text: Pankaj Singh Pundir, popularly known as Sher Singh Rana or S. Rana, is an Indian politician born on 17 May 1976 in a Hindu Rajput family in Roorkee, Uttarakhand, India.[8][9] He was sentenced in August 2014 to life imprisonment and a fine of ₹100,000 (approximately US$1,600) for the 2001 assassination of Phoolan Devi, a dacoit-turned-parliamentarian who was a sitting Member of Parliament in the 13th Lok Sabha, along with charges of conspiracy after a 10-year trial.[5][6] Rana, along with two other men, murdered Phoolan Devi outside her home in New Delhi in July 2001, claiming revenge for her actions as a leader of a bandit gang that targeted higher castes in the late 1970s and early 1980s. He was arrested and confessed to the murder.[11][12] On 17 February 2004, Rana escaped from Tihar jail, a high-security prison in Delhi, went to Moradabad, checked into a hotel, and received ₹1 lakh from relatives. From Ranchi, he applied for a passport in the name of Sanjay Gupta.[14] During a two-month wait for the passport, he visited Gaya and Benaras, then went to Kolkata where he obtained a three-month Bangladesh visa. Rana claimed he rented a house in Khulna and lived there posing as Sanjay Gupta. After fleeing to Bangladesh, he bought a satellite phone for ₹16,500 to contact relatives and friends without being tracked. He traveled from Moradabad to Ranchi, Kolkata, Bangladesh, Dubai, and later to Afghanistan, where he is said to have brought back the ashes of the Rajput king Prithviraj Chauhan.[17] He received approximately ₹15,000 to ₹20,000 per month and visited Kolkata regularly to extend his visa, sometimes in Dhaka.[18] On 25 April 2006, he was re-arrested in Kolkata by the SIT, who tracked him down through his subscription to a Hindi newspaper, one of the few people in the Dharmatala area who did so.[19][20] In January 2012, a trial court allowed Rana to file nomination papers from Tihar to contest the Uttar Pradesh assembly election.[21] The Delhi High Court granted him bail, and he was released on 24 October 2016.[22] On 28 February 2018, he married Pratima Singh, daughter of Pratap Singh; however, some newspapers incorrectly stated that Pratap Singh was a former Member of Legislative Assembly from Madhya Pradesh; in fact, Rekha Yadav was the MLA from Malhara in 2008.[23] The marriage was conducted with a shagun of only a silver coin and without accepting a dowry of 10 crore rupees worth property and 31 lakh rupees in cash.[24][25][26] In 2019, Rana formed his own political party, the Rashtravadi Janlok Party (RJP).[27]
